justification_text:
My point estimates reflect a broadly stable near-term outlook with a mild upward drift over time. At the one-day horizon, the estimate of 272.5 is essentially anchored to the most recent observed price or level, with very little expected movement given typical short-run momentum and mean-reversion dynamics. At the one-week horizon, I nudged the estimate slightly higher to 273.0, reflecting a marginal positive drift assumption consistent with modest underlying trend. At the one-month horizon, the estimate rises to 275.0, incorporating a slightly more pronounced drift while still remaining conservative — the idea being that over a month, there is some expected appreciation but not a dramatic departure from current levels. In all three cases, I was not incorporating any strong directional signal, so the estimates cluster tightly around the current level.

The confidence interval widths expand meaningfully as the horizon lengthens, which is the natural consequence of uncertainty compounding over time. At one day, the 90% interval of 265–280 spans roughly 15 points, reflecting that daily moves are relatively contained under normal market conditions. By one week, the interval widens to 259–287, a 28-point range, capturing the possibility of a few consecutive adverse or favorable sessions. At one month, the interval stretches to 248–302, a 54-point range, acknowledging that over a month's time, sentiment shifts, macro data surprises, and technical level breaks can produce substantially larger cumulative moves. The asymmetry is intentional but modest — I did not see strong skew signals, so the intervals are roughly symmetric around the point estimates.

Several specific risks could push outcomes outside even these wider intervals. On the downside, a sharp deterioration in macroeconomic data — such as a worse-than-expected inflation print, a sudden credit event, or a geopolitical escalation — could trigger a rapid de-risking move that pushes the level well below the lower bound of the one-month interval. On the upside, an unexpectedly dovish policy pivot, a strong earnings or economic surprise, or a short-squeeze dynamic in a thinly traded environment could push the level above 302. Liquidity conditions also matter: if market depth is thin, moves can overshoot fundamental fair value by a wide margin before correcting. These tail events are not captured fully within a 90% interval by construction, and I would assign a combined roughly 10% probability to outcomes outside the stated ranges at each horizon.
